title: Wannier-Stark localization, confinement and edge states
authors: N. Aucar Boidi, A. Aharony, O. Entin-Wohlman, C. Proetto
abstract: The boundary between a system's bulk and the vacuum can be modeled by a potential which confines the electrons to the bulk. Here we present the example of the Wannier-Stark linear potential, generated by an electric field along one axis of a two-dimensional lattice. Along that axis, the potential generates electronic states which are localized around each lattice site, with eigenenergies which form the Wannier-Stark ladder. In the transverse direction, the states are governed by a tight binding model with free Bloch states. In the ground state, filling these states under the Pauli principle generates an insulating bulk and an edge which can be metallic in the transverse direction. This paper explains the concepts of localization, localization length, filling and confinement. The paper also acquaints the readers with the use of Bessel functions in the solution of a simple physical model. These topics can be easily included in courses on solid state physics, and only require prior knowledge of quantum mechanics.
summary: This paper analyzes electron localization in lattices subjected to an electric field via the Wannier-Stark potential. It mathematically derives that these states are localized (Bessel functions), leading to insulating bulk behavior. By extending the model to 2D, it demonstrates how this confinement can create distinct metallic edge states alongside an insulating interior.
main_problem: The paper investigates Wannier-Stark localization, confinement, and the resulting edge states that appear at the boundary between a bulk material and vacuum when subjected to an electric field.
main_result: In 1D, the system is always insulating due to localized Wannier-Stark states; however, extending to 2D allows for the construction of models exhibiting both an insulating bulk and potentially metallic edge states.
method: The analysis relies on solving tight-binding Hamiltonians in the presence of a linear potential, leading to eigenfunctions expressible in terms of Bessel functions.
model_or_system: The model is non-interacting electrons on a 2D lattice subjected to a Wannier-Stark potential generated by an electric field along one axis. The physics transitions from 1D chains (analyzed via recurrence relations) to 2D lattices with transverse tunneling.
key_observables: Localization length ($\xi$), electron occupation profile $n(j;x)$, and the energy spectrum showing discrete Wannier-Stark levels coupled to continuous transverse bands.
important_parameters: The dimensionless parameter $x = 2t/(eaF)$ controls the degree of localization, with limits analyzed for large ($x 	o \infty$) and small ($x 	o 0$) electric fields.
main_assumptions: Initially assumes non-interacting electrons; later incorporates electron-electron interactions (Hubbard/nearest-neighbor) to study correlated effects near the edge.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the localization of states in 1D, the occupation profile decaying across an edge region at half-filling, and the resulting energy band structure in 2D.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the 1D Wannier-Stark ladder using Bessel functions to analyzing the many-electron filling (insulating bulk) before extending the formalism to a 2D lattice model that reveals metallic edge possibilities.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, solvable model for how external fields can induce topological or boundary phenomena in condensed matter systems, which is highly relevant for understanding engineered quantum materials and interfaces.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. A sketch of the one-dimensional lattice, represented by the dotted circles along the horizontal axis, with an odd number of sites placed in a linear potential µ j = eaF j. Each step indicates the energy of the corresponding site due to the presence of the potential which vanishes at the central site of the chain j = 0. Electrons can hop between neighboring sites with energy t.

FIG. 2. (Color online) Probability nj = Jj(x)2 of finding a single electron in the Wannier-Stark eigenstate ℓ= 0, as a function of site index j, for several values of the electric fields F, in units of t/(ea). These states are localized around the cite j = 0. The full lines connect the actual values, which are calculated only for integer j. The straight segments signal the value of the localization length 2ξ = 4t/(eF).
FIG. 3. (Color online) Occupation number profile for different values of x, Eq. (13). The squares indicate the distance ξ from the origin, see Eq. (9).

FIG. 4. The energy levels of the two-dimensional case, with M = 5, N′ = 5, Eq. (16). The horizontal axis denotes the index ℓ, which is also equal to the horizontal site index around which the corre- sponding states are localized, j = ℓ. The thick segments represent the Wannier-Stark ladder. Each of these energies is “dressed" by a band of N′ levels, representing the band of “free" electronic states in the transverse direction. The width of such a band is indicated by the double headed vertical arrow.
